THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA
ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Smt.Mohana Kumari, learned counsel who represents Sri.Abubacker Shafi, learned counsel on record for the appellant.

Also heard Sri.Sunil Kumar K., learned counsel who represents Sri.Lingaraj H.S., learned counsel on record for respondent No.1.
2.
The appellant who sustained injuries in a road traffic accident filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in total.
The Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Devanahalli, which dealt with the matter as MVC No.60/2016 rendered orders on 06.11.2019 awarding a sum of Rs.1,69,700/- as compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is preferred.
3. Smt.Mohana Kumari, learned counsel for the appellant contends that the appellant sustained grievous NC: 2024:KHC:45641 injuries in a road traffic accident.
The appellant due to the injuries sustained became permanently and completely disabled.
However, the Tribunal did not award any sum as compensation under the head loss of future earnings.
Learned counsel also states that the amount awarded under all other heads is also grossly low.
Learned counsel thereby seeks for enhancement of compensation.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel Sri.Sunil Kumar K., representing respondent No.1 submits that the appellant took treatment as inpatient for a period of three days only.
The accident occurred in the year 2015.
For the relevant period the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,69,700/- as compensation which is highly excessive and therefore, the present appeal is not maintainable.
5. A perusal of record reveals that the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,69,667/- as compensation divided under the following heads.

sentences.text: Undisputedly, the appellant sustained comminuted type-II fracture of shaft of right femur which is grievous in nature.
Also by the contents of Ex.P11 discharge summary it is clear that the appellant underwent a procedure i.e. IMIL Nailing to the injured femur.
However, the appellant failed to produce any evidence to establish the aspect of disability.

Without there being any proof that there is permanent and physical disability in respect of whole body, one cannot expect the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal to award compensation towards loss of future earnings.
However, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- only under the head traveling, food, nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental expenses.
Also the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.18,000/- only towards loss of income during the period of treatment.
7. The version of the appellant as per his claim application is that, as agriculturist he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
However, the appellant did not produce any proof NC: 2024:KHC:45641 either in respect of his occupation or earnings by the date of accident.
But, having considered the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the view that the appellant would have taken bed rest atleast for a period of three months.

Therefore, globally this Court considers desirable to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- in addition to the sum that is awarded by the Tribunal as compensation so as to make the sum that the appellant would be paid as compensation, will be justifiable.
Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Devanahalli, through orders in MVC No.60/2016 dated 6.11.2019 is enhanced by Rs.25,000/-.
iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

3 v)
On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.
